patterns.canonical_text:
(?x)
  "                     # opening quote
  (?<key> [^"\\]+ )     # the key text (no escape handling, kept simple)
  "
  \s* : \s*             # colon separator, optional surrounding whitespace

(?x)        # turn on extended mode
  -?        # an optional minus
  (?:
    0       # a zero
    |       # ...or...
    [1-9]   # a 1-9 character
    \d*     # followed by zero or more digits
  )
  (?:
    (?:
      \.    # a period
      \d+   # followed by one or more digits
    )?
    (?:
      [eE]  # an e character
      [+-]? # followed by an option +/-
      \d+   # followed by one or more digits
    )?      # make exponent optional
  )?        # make decimal portion optional

(?x)                # turn on extended mode
  \\                # a literal backslash
  (?:               # ...followed by...
    ["\\/bfnrt]     # one of these characters
    |               # ...or...
    u               # a u
    [0-9a-fA-F]{4}) # and four hex digits

subbench.objective: A CAPABILITY CONTRAST across the [B7] engine roster: what each engine can EXPRESS, what it REFUSES, and what the expressible patterns COST -- over a set built from real, deployed regex shapes wherever a permissive-licensed source could be fetched (OWASP's validation repository and CRS ruleset, Elastic's grok patterns, rebar's wild corpora, VS Code's JSON grammar, PCRE2's and rust-regex's own test corpora) and authored fresh, held to the SAME realism rule, where none exists (backreference, lookaround, recursion, ReDoS and non-UTF-8 shapes a real author would plausibly write for that purpose -- Frank's Q2 ruling, 2026-09-12: 'from the wild' is a REALISM framing, not a ratio to hit). BUILT ON pcrec's `.rxt` format as this set's pattern source of truth (Frank's Q3 ruling), the first pcrec-bench set authored that way. See docs/design/capability_set_v1.md and NOTES.md.
